title: beads-bootstrap.sh rm -rf's local engine gated only on a local '0' count — verify recoverability BEFORE deleting
description:
scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh runs automatically every SessionStart (via install-bd.sh). When 'bd stats' reports 0 issues it executes 'rm -rf .beads/embeddeddolt .beads/dolt' and THEN tries 'bd bootstrap' to pull from origin. It never verifies origin actually carries refs/dolt/data before deleting. Combined with Bench-h4f (origin often has no ref), this is a latent data-loss hazard: 'delete, then hope'. (Note: it removes only the engine subdirs and guards on '[ -d .beads ]', so it cannot delete .beads/ wholesale — scope the fix to the engine-clear path.)

Acceptance criteria:
- Invert the order: prove a recovery source exists (origin refs/dolt/data reachable, OR a non-empty committed .beads/issues.jsonl) BEFORE removing any engine dir.
- If neither source exists, refuse to clear and log a loud warning; leave the (possibly cold) local engine intact.
- Red test: with bd stats=0 and origin carrying NO refs/dolt/data and no committed issues.jsonl, the script must NOT rm the engine dirs and must exit non-destructively.

title: bench:init never establishes refs/dolt/data on origin — local-only boards have no rehydrate source
description:
Bench's entire rehydrate model assumes 'reachable Dolt history lives on git origin under refs/dolt/data' (stated in scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh). But nothing in commands/init.md, templates/CLAUDE.bench.md, or any script ever runs 'bd dolt remote add' or 'bd dolt push'. The ONLY code that creates refs/dolt/data is scripts/beads-cloud-push.sh, which is web-only (gated on CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true). Net: a local-only Bench user never gets a portable rehydrate source, so every cold-board bootstrap is an unrecoverable no-op.

Acceptance criteria:
- bench:init Step 2 configures a Dolt remote (origin) and performs an initial 'bd dolt push' so refs/dolt/data exists from day one.
- init verifies .beads/issues.jsonl is COMMITTED (not merely staged).
- A non-web local SessionEnd path keeps origin's refs/dolt/data current (generalize beads-cloud-push.sh or add a local equivalent).
- Red test: a fresh 'bench:init' in a repo with an origin results in 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' returning a ref.

title: Local board reversion: .beads git hooks auto-import stale committed issues.jsonl on worktree-add/merge
description: Observed live 2026-07-03: 'bd close Bench-uba' succeeded, but after the orchestrator created a scratch integration worktree (git worktree add -> post-checkout hook) and merged 4 feature branches in it (git merge x4 -> post-merge hook), Bench-uba reverted to its Jun-29 OPEN row (Updated timestamp regressed; the close event vanished). Rows created after the trigger survived (import doesn't delete unknown rows); rows whose committed-jsonl snapshot was stale got clobbered. This is the LOCAL twin of the cloud reversion bug fixed by beads-cloud-push.sh: bd's own .beads/hooks (post-checkout/post-merge run 'bd hooks run <name>') treat the committed .beads/issues.jsonl as an import source, and every feature branch/worktree carries a stale snapshot. The bench-orchestrator SKILL.md footgun section warns against HAND-merging jsonl but not about bd's own hooks re-importing on checkout/merge. ## Repro hypothesis 1. - doctor reports global/shared-engine usage as a warning with the repo-local remediation.

title: worktree-reap: CURRENT_TREE guard ineffective when invoked with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set
description: Pre-existing latent bug (predates chore/consistency-sweep; identical on main). worktree-reap.sh does 'cd "$ROOT"' (=CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) before computing CURRENT_TREE via 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel', so CURRENT_TREE always resolves to the MAIN tree, not the tree the caller was standing in. Effect: if the reaper is run from *inside* a worktree whose branch is merged (or HEAD unreachable), the [ "$wt_path" = "$CURRENT_TREE" ] guard never matches and the live tree is reaped out from under the caller. Not reachable on the wired SessionStart path (cwd = project root, so MAIN_TREE guard covers it), which is why it's low priority. The consistency-sweep case-widening ('$WT_DIR'/* instead of agent-*/wf_*) broadens the off-path blast radius of this bug (any-named tree now reapable-from-inside, not just agent-/wf_), motivating a fix. Repro: run reaper with cwd inside .claude/worktrees/<merged-tree> and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<project root> -> the tree is removed. Fix: capture CURRENT_TREE from the caller's cwd before 'cd "$ROOT"', or resolve it via $PWD's git-common-dir, and keep the MAIN_TREE guard as a second line of defense. Surfaced during review of Bench-z0v.
